clue.text: Island fish — fuss to get caught

indicators.note: something caught is held inside, so the fuss sits within the fish

parts.note: barbs are freshwater fish of the carp family
ado means fuss or bother

explanation.surface: An angler on an island makes a great to-do about landing a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbados is a Caribbean nation occupying a single island in the Lesser Antilles.

clue.text: Flower distributor

definitions.meaning: something that flows, here a river
The giant online retailer that ships goods out

explanation.surface: A florist's wholesale supplier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is read as 'one that flows', the old crossword trick for a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Amazon is South America's great river, and Amazon the company distributes goods worldwide.

clue.text: Encouragement to give good person a bad time?

parts.note: to give someone a bad time is to boo them; with 'give' as the link the phrase stands for a jeer
ST, short for saint, is the usual crossword good person

explanation.surface: A cheeky suggestion that tormenting a do-gooder is a kind of encouragement.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer splits as an instruction: jeer at a saint. 'give ... a bad time' wraps round 'good person' in the surface, but the jeer still comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A boost is a lift in morale, the encouragement that spurs someone on.

clue.text: Fab change to catch upper-class cheat

parts.note: def is slang for excellent, as is fab

indicators.note: to catch something is to hold it, so the class letter goes inside

parts.note: to alter is to change

explanation.surface: A posh swindler changes his story to something fab.
explanation.definitionFit: A defaulter fails to pay what is owed, a kind of cheat in money matters.

clue.text: One on their feet somehow needs a rest ultimately

indicators.note: somehow tells us the letters reach the answer by some rearranged route
ultimately points to the final letter of the word rest

explanation.surface: Someone standing for ages eventually has to sit down.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram indicator is the clue's fourth word; it rearranges NEEDS A plus T, the final letter of 'rest' given by 'ultimately'.
explanation.definitionFit: A standee is a person who stands, as in a theatre or on a crowded bus with no seat.

clue.text: European holding party sent around lackey

indicators.note: holding means the first word keeps the second inside it

parts.note: a Pole is a European

indicators.note: sent around says the word for party is turned to face the other way

parts.note: a do is a party

explanation.surface: A European on his way back from a party is accompanied by a servant.
explanation.definitionFit: A poodle is slang for a servile follower, the obedient pet of someone powerful.

clue.text: Factory's undercover agent?

definitions.meaning: a spy placed secretly inside an organisation

explanation.surface: A spy embedded in a factory.
explanation.definitionFit: Plant means both an industrial works and a person planted secretly to gather information.

clue.text: Lapse during the hours of darkness — change of direction taking place inside

indicators.text: change of direction taking place inside
indicators.note: one compass point within the word is swapped for its opposite, north giving way to south

parts.note: overnight means during the night

explanation.surface: A night-time slip-up while a ship turns course.
explanation.walkthrough: The N (north) inside is replaced by S (south), the 'change of direction'.
explanation.definitionFit: An oversight is an unintended failure to notice something, a lapse of attention.

clue.text: Soho celebrity here is playing harmoniously

indicators.note: playing signals the letters are rearranged, as a band improvises

parts.note: the long word holding both the answer's letters and those of Soho

explanation.surface: A star of London's Soho is performing in perfect harmony.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite: the letters of SOHO plus the answer ('here') rearranged ('playing') make HARMONIOUSLY; take SOHO's letters out of HARMONIOUSLY and rearrange the rest. Soho is a London district famed for nightlife.
explanation.definitionFit: A luminary is a person of eminence who shines in their field, a famous figure.

clue.text: Sunday — with such a break you should get sun!

definitions.text: Sunday — with such a break you should get sun!

parts.words: Sunday — with such a break you should get sun!
parts.note: the word Sunday with its last three letters taken away leaves sun, and that removal is also a holiday from work

explanation.surface: Take a Sunday off and you'll enjoy some sunshine.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: take DAY OFF 'Sunday' and SUN is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A day off is a break from work, and Sunday is the classic one.

clue.text: A learner into an Austen novel — one displays 'sunny' disposition

indicators.note: into means the first pieces go inside the others

parts.note: taken as written
Emma is a novel by Jane Austen
L is for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A student is slotted into an Austen novel, displaying a cheerful nature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sunny' disposition means the arrangement of the sun's positions, not a cheerful temperament.
explanation.definitionFit: An analemma is the figure-of-eight curve showing the sun's position in the sky at one time of day over a year.

clue.text: City walked about with hillock — nothing standing out

indicators.note: about here means turned round, the past tense read backwards

parts.note: trod means walked

indicators.note: standing out means left out, so the zero letter is dropped

parts.note: a mound is a hillock
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A traveller walked about a city and its little hill, with nothing remarkable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses TROD to DORT; MOUND loses its O as 'nothing standing out'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dortmund is a major industrial city in Germany's Ruhr region.

clue.text: Poetic comment when identifying a recreational tablet in drink?

parts.note: 'tis is the poetic form of it is, what one says on identifying something
an is a form of a
E is slang for an ecstasy tablet

explanation.surface: A poet spots a party pill dropped into someone's drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The contraction for 'it is' survives mainly in verse, hence 'Poetic'; 'recreational tablet' is drug slang for ecstasy.
explanation.definitionFit: A tisane is a herbal infusion, a hot drink made from leaves or flowers.

clue.text: Helpful senior person who could bring pax for British Latinists?

parts.words: who could bring pax for British Latinists
parts.note: split as PA X, the Latin word for peace becomes a dad followed by the Roman numeral ten

explanation.surface: A kindly elder who brings peace to a classics society.
explanation.walkthrough: PAX splits as PA (father) and X (a figure, Roman ten), so the answer 'could bring' pax; 'British' because pa for father is British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A father figure is an older person looked up to for guidance and support, like a parent.

clue.text: Take account of good business involving debts

parts.note: to factor in something is to take account of it

explanation.surface: Consider a sound firm that deals in debts.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrasal verb 'factor in' supplies all but the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Factoring is the trade of buying a company's unpaid invoices at a discount and collecting them.

clue.text: Part of Netherlands gets very hot — come to the coast?

parts.note: someone who fries in the sun gets very hot
to land is to come ashore

explanation.surface: A Dutch region sweltering, so people head for the seaside.
explanation.definitionFit: Friesland is a northern province of the Netherlands, on the North Sea coast.

clue.text: Bait chum in trouble? It's somewhat unreasonable

indicators.note: in trouble suggests the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Teasing a friend in difficulty seems rather unfair.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling something a bit much means it is excessive, rather more than is fair.

clue.text: Enlightenment certainly doesn't come easily from one finding subtractions tricky

definitions.text: Enlightenment certainly doesn't come easily from one

indicators.note: tricky suggests the letters are dodgy and must be reworked

explanation.surface: Someone baffled by take-away sums is slow to be enlightened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Enlightenment' is the learning sense, not the historical movement; the definition is a whimsical description.
explanation.definitionFit: An obscurantist deliberately opposes knowledge and keeps things vague, so they impart no understanding.

clue.text: Spooner's comic panto figure, no reason to celebrate!

indicators.note: Spooner, the don famed for swapping word starts, signals an exchange of initial sounds

parts.note: the dame is the comic cross-dressed role in British pantomime
nay means no

explanation.surface: A pantomime dame turns out to be no cause for festivity.
explanation.walkthrough: The pantomime is a British Christmas stage show for families, in which the 'dame' is a man in drag.
explanation.definitionFit: A name day is the feast of the saint one is named after, celebrated like a birthday.

clue.text: Reckon like tot finishing with toe

parts.note: as means like
a tot is a sum, as in tot up

indicators.note: finishing with points to the end letter of the word toe

explanation.surface: A toddler's guess, ending with a toe.
explanation.definitionFit: To assume is to suppose or take for granted, to reckon something is so.

clue.text: Biological tissue destroyed in a storm

indicators.note: destroyed means the letters are wrecked and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Living tissue ruined in a storm.
explanation.definitionFit: Stroma is the supporting framework tissue of an organ, or the matrix within a chloroplast.

clue.text: The female embraced by a knight is looking pallid

indicators.note: embraced by means held inside the following pieces

parts.note: N is the chess notation for a knight
she is the female pronoun

explanation.surface: A woman hugged by a knight turns pale.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashen means grey like ash, the pale colour of someone in shock.

clue.text: What's emerged from referendum is — h'm! — a shambolic mess

indicators.note: what emerges from these words is a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: Wry comment that a referendum result has been a chaotic mess.
explanation.definitionFit: A mishmash is a confused jumble, a disordered muddle.

clue.text: Almost all book up, wanting the Spanish stopover?

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters climb, read backwards
almost all means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a tome is a book
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Almost all the rooms booked, and no Spanish to be had at the inn?
explanation.definitionFit: A motel is a roadside hotel, a place to stop over on a journey.

clue.text: Joke I poured forth heckled by the audience?

parts.note: a pun is a play on words, a joke
to shed is to pour forth or give off

explanation.surface: A comedian's pun falls flat and the crowd heckles.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose, hence the question mark: heckling is a punishment for a weak joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer jeered by the crowd is in effect penalised, paying for a bad routine.

clue.text: Film director's arrogance shown when dismissing the lead

indicators.note: dismissing the lead means the opening letter goes

parts.note: hauteur is haughty arrogance

explanation.surface: A director's arrogance shows when he fires his leading actor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' looks like the star actor, but it is the first letter, H.
explanation.definitionFit: An auteur is a film-maker whose personal style marks their films as their own creative work.

clue.text: Military commander, wasting little time, fired weapon

indicators.note: wasting means losing, so the time letter is lost

parts.note: a shotgun is a weapon that is fired
T is the short form of time

explanation.surface: A general wastes no time and fires his gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A shogun was a hereditary military ruler of feudal Japan.

clue.text: Sang and cried about love and died

indicators.note: about means the shout surrounds the other letters

parts.note: yelled means cried out
love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A lovesick singer wails about lost love and death.
explanation.definitionFit: To yodel is to sing with rapid switches between chest voice and falsetto, an Alpine singing style.
